claim: Existing LLM trading-agent research has weak reproducibility and protocol comparability
evidence_summary: P001 reports 77 included studies, 19 primary empirical studies, only 2/19 time-consistent split protocols, 1/19 explicit transaction-cost model, 1/19 universe/survivorship handling, and no R3 reproducibility.
next_verification_needed: Extract full paper tables and definitions for reproducibility coding

claim: Current LLM agents still struggle with real-world expert-authored finance research tasks
evidence_summary: P013 reports 537 expert-authored questions using SEC filings and an agentic harness; best model OpenAI o3 achieved 46.8 percent accuracy at USD 3.79 per query.
current_confidence: High for benchmarked finance research questions
next_verification_needed: Extract task taxonomy and scoring protocol from full text

claim: Investment research agents are a distinct category from trading agents
evidence_summary: P013 focuses on financial research questions and P016 focuses on equity research and valuation; P001 focuses on trading agents. This suggests a meaningful distinction, but formal definition is still needed.
next_verification_needed: Define investment research agent precisely and test against included papers

claim: Auditability is underdeveloped in LLM-based financial agents
evidence_summary: Existing evidence indicates reproducibility/evaluation limitations, but direct auditability coding has not yet been systematically extracted.
next_verification_needed: Create auditability coding rules and score at least 20 papers

claim: Risk-first evaluation is a necessary next direction
evidence_summary: P001 shows weak transaction-cost and survivorship reporting; P014 includes governance framing; P015 motivates hedging and volatility robustness. Need more direct risk-first literature extraction.
next_verification_needed: Verify P010 and extract risk metrics across top papers

evidence_summary: This is the project's strategic synthesis, not yet a fully proven claim. It is supported by reproducibility gaps, real-world research-task difficulty, benchmarking lifecycle concerns, and equity research agent direction.
